captures.what_is_new: The Parliament's own summary (updated 25 Oct 2026): proposal 19 Nov 2025, provisional agreement 7 May 2026, plenary approval 16 June (423 for, 57 against, 174 abstentions), Council adoption 29 June, signature 8 July, publication 24 July as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; fixed deadlines for high-risk rules (2 December 2027 stand-alone, 2 August 2028 embedded in products); the duty to mark AI-generated content postponed to 2 December 2026 for systems on the market before 2 August 2026; a new prohibition on AI practices generating non-consensual intimate or sexual content and child sexual abuse material; a simplified registration duty for non-high-risk systems; the strict-necessity standard for special-category data used for bias correction reinstated; simplified documentation for medium-sized companies kept; stronger AI Office powers; AI-enabled machinery taken out of the direct high-risk regime. The Parliament's description, not the legal text.

The Commission's questions and answers (updated 20 Oct 2026): the delay in standards put the 2 August 2026 start of the high-risk rules in jeopardy; the Omnibus extends the dates (2 December 2027; 2 August 2028 for products such as medical devices, toys and lifts); it entered into force on 27 July 2026; standards are voluntary but decisive for legal certainty; the extra time is for standards and national authorities. Read only for the timeline and standards.

story_candidates.title: How the EU simplified the AI Act: what changed and when

ai_path.connection: Direct: the EU's AI regulation and its amendment (the Digital Omnibus on AI).
ai_path.places: The European Union and its Member States (national authorities and conformity assessment bodies).

story_candidates.angle: The EU amended its AI Act through the Digital Omnibus on AI, proposed on 19 November 2025 and published as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 on 24 July 2026. According to the Parliament and the Commission, the high-risk rules now apply from 2 December 2027, or 2 August 2028 for AI built into products, because the standards were late, the duty to mark AI-generated content moved to 2 December 2026 for older systems, and the Act gained a ban on AI practices that generate non-consensual intimate content and child sexual abuse material, with lighter registration and documentation for some companies and stronger powers for the AI Office.
story_candidates.note: For journalist-europe. Ready. Conditions: re-read both pages yourself; attribute each change to the Parliament's page or the Commission's (their descriptions, not the legal text, which was not read: say so, and link the Official Journal only if you read it); give the dates as the pages give them, and the vote count as the Parliament's; the Parliament says publication 24 July as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and the Commission says the Omnibus 'entered into force on 27 July 2026': say both as theirs; do not give costs, savings or what companies will do (neither page was read for that); say what the pages say each change is for (standards and national authorities were late) and do not add your own view; S50 already carries the 2 December 2027 date for high-risk rules in sensitive areas: link to it and do not repeat its content; explain 'high-risk AI system', 'standards', 'conformity assessment body' and 'AI Office' in plain words at first use; the AI connection (direct, 0 steps) goes in the data note; length follows the story (usually 400 to 900 words for analysis, 300 to 700 for news); categories Europe and AI.
